definitions.explanation: The first day of the work week in Japan. The kanji 月 means 'moon' and relates to the Latin 'Luna' for Monday.

examples.japanese: {月曜日|げつようび}に{会|あ}いましょう。
{今日|きょう}は{月曜日|げつようび}です。
{月曜日|げつようび}から{金曜日|きんようび}まで{働|はたら}きます。
examples.english: I work from Monday to Friday.

examples.japanese: {月曜日|げつようび}は{仕事|しごと}が{多|おお}いので、いつも{忙|いそが}しいです。
examples.english: Monday is always busy because there's a lot of work.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}は{休|やす}みなので、{友達|ともだち}と{出|で}かける{予定|よてい}です。
examples.english: Next Monday is a holiday, so I'm planning to go out with a friend.

notes:
{月曜日|げつようび} means Monday - the first day of the work week in Japan.

DAYS OF THE WEEK:
All end with {曜日|ようび} (day of the week):
- {月曜日|げつようび}: Monday ({月|つき} = moon)
- {火曜日|かようび}: Tuesday ({火|ひ} = fire)
- {水曜日|すいようび}: Wednesday ({水|みず} = water)
- {木曜日|もくようび}: Thursday ({木|き} = tree)
- {金曜日|きんようび}: Friday ({金|きん} = gold/metal)
- {土曜日|どようび}: Saturday ({土|つち} = earth)
- {日曜日|にちようび}: Sunday ({日|ひ} = sun)

ABBREVIATION:
Can be shortened to {月曜|げつよう} in casual speech or schedules.

USAGE:
- {月曜日|げつようび}に: on Monday
- {毎週|まいしゅう}{月曜日|げつようび}: every Monday
- {来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}: next Monday

ETYMOLOGY:
The kanji {月|つき} (moon) relates to Latin 'Luna' - Monday means 'Moon day' in both languages.
